lesson: A later checkpoint with identical or worse correctness but much larger score magnitude is not automatically better. Treat confidence growth without generalization growth as a possible overconfidence failure and preserve the earlier checkpoint for repair if novel evaluation supports it.
Failure-driven repair should generate new analogous training examples rather than train on the frozen evaluation cases that exposed the failure. Keep challenge contamination boundaries explicit.
implementation: 30-row targeted repair bank; 20 train and 10 held-out dev across five observed failure families; frozen novel challenge remains eval-only.

lesson: For a bounded repair, selective upper-layer tuning plus replay can change model behavior without increasing the deployed graph. Efficiency constraints should shape the repair itself, not be postponed to serving optimization.

Do not confuse frontier awareness with architecture churn. Keep a strong current Pareto architecture when it fits the workload; place newer families on a measured ablation watchlist and switch only when the product bottleneck is demonstrated.

Interactive AI needs an explicit fast path. Avoid full-history recomputation, unbounded candidate reranking, routine long-context use, and repeated judge loops. Retrieval/caching and small rerank budgets often matter more to product latency than swapping the core architecture.

MC10D-style infrastructure capture is a project failure mode. Validation should protect imminent model/data/product work; repeated infrastructure qualification without new capability work is forbidden.

Distributed training schedule semantics are part of model correctness. When Accelerate wraps a scheduler with non-split batches, preserve global optimizer-step meaning using the already-proven scheduler-step translation rather than silently compressing warmup/decay.
